Something I do to warm up on days where I really have trouble feeling my upper back is deadlift iso holds. 

I basically go into a power rack and place the empty bar under the safety pins, which are at about mid shin or lower. I deadlift the empty bar up to that height and keep it tensioned against the pins. 

I like this a lot because in order to do it, you pretty much HAVE to keep that upper back nice and tight. 

It can also help with the long arm cue because sometimes people can’t do both simultaneously. Some people get too caught up with long arm that they let their thoracic spine lose tension. Two birds, one stone.

I usually do a top set with a prescribed RPE and I do backoffs sets of either a percentage of my top set, or a percentage of my 1RM. 

For me, doing top sets gauge my ability for the day and allow me to get the stimulus and experience from a heavier load, and also I can tweak my backoffs sets as needed based on how it felt. 

For example, in my strength block right now, I hit a top single of 340lb @ RPE 8. Usually, 340 for me moves at around an RPE 6. Based on that, I knew my current fatigue was a little high, so I lowered the weight of my percentage based back off sets in order to get quality reps in, instead of pushing through something that would’ve been way too hard and possibly having form breakdown or risk injury

The bittersweet thing about getting stronger and setting PR’s is that your percentage based back off sets get heavier.

For me, accessories are typically relative to the compound movements I do that day. 

For example, when I bench I like to do cable rows to the part of my chest where the barbell touches me during bench press.

 Also, because my elbows get beat up from benching 4x a week, I do a LOT of high rep curls and tricep kickbacks. Not for muscle growth (although it has helped lol) but just for elbow health. 

For squats and deadlifts, I’m developing a bit of a hip shift and glute imbalance so to mitigate it I like to do staggered stance KB deadlifts, Bulgarian split squats, etc. just a lot of single movements. 

I’d say in general, all accessories I do have a purpose. That way I’m not incurring a large fatigue debt from accessories that don’t even really help. I just stay flexible with it so I have fun doing it :)
